title: Achieve at least 20% mean weight loss with an approved incretin treatment

concept.text: Produce substantial, sustained weight reduction during pharmacological treatment of obesity. Semaglutide established roughly 15% mean loss, and tirzepatide achieved 20.9% at 72 weeks in SURMOUNT-1. Proposed completion test: FDA chronic weight-management approval supported by a randomized phase 3 trial demonstrating at least 20% mean baseline weight reduction at approximately 72 weeks in adults without diabetes, with superiority to placebo under an estimand that includes treatment discontinuation. Test set by: FDA sets approval; SURMOUNT-1 investigators prespecified the trial endpoints and estimands. The 20% boundary is an editorial breakthrough threshold, not an FDA approval requirement. Reported achieved: FDA approved tirzepatide (Zepbound) on 8 November 2023, following SURMOUNT-1; semaglutide (Wegovy) received chronic weight-management approval on 4 June 2021. Overlaps: END-05. Sources given: [FDA Wegovy approval announcement](https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/USFDA/bulletins/2e2adc7) ; [FDA Zepbound approval announcement](https://www.fda.gov/news-events/press-announcements/fda-approves-new-medication-chronic-weight-management) ; [SURMOUNT-1 primary publication](https://www.darmzentrum-bern.ch/fileadmin/darmzentrum/Education/Journal_Club/2022/JC-22-07-20_NEJM_Tirzepatide_Once_Weekly_for_the_Treatment.pdf).

page.title: Obesity medicine matching the weight loss of bariatric surgery
page.definition: Adults assigned to an approved obesity medicine lose at least 25% of their starting body weight on average at 72 weeks or later, including those who stop taking it. The trial includes adults without type 2 diabetes who have obesity or have overweight with a weight-related complication. The 25% benchmark describes the approximate loss maintained for up to 10 years after gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy. The comparison is limited to the amount of weight lost.

goal.need: In 2024, 940 million adults worldwide lived with obesity. Diet and exercise interventions averaged 7.4% weight loss in a systematic review. Some complications may require much larger losses: sustained loss of 25–30% may resolve obesity hypoventilation syndrome, although the evidence is uncertain. In 2022, US bariatric procedures numbered about 1% of the population eligible by body mass index. A medicine would give people who need substantial weight loss an option without surgery. Keeping the weight off may require continued treatment.

statements.body: European Association for the Study of Obesity, Obesity Management Task Force
statements.quote: A greater (20% or more) weight loss may be considered for those with greater degrees of obesity
statements.context: The passage specifies BMI ≥35 kg/m². BMI is weight in kilograms divided by height in metres squared. This is an individual treatment objective without a specified drug or population mean.

statements.quote: surgical procedures accomplish weight loss and improve health outcomes as targets for developing new pharmacologic therapies.
statements.context: The Strategic Plan for NIH Obesity Research calls for studying the mechanisms of bariatric procedures to identify drug targets. It gives no numerical weight-loss threshold for a medicine.

completion.title: An approved obesity medicine produces at least 25% mean weight loss in a phase 3 trial.
completion.criterion: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial, adults without type 2 diabetes have obesity or have overweight with a weight-related complication. At least 72 weeks after randomization, the estimated mean loss from randomization in one drug-dose group is at least 25% of baseline body weight. The estimate includes all participants assigned to that group, regardless of discontinuation. The FDA or European Commission has approved the medicine at that dose for chronic weight management. The approved prescribing information or a peer-reviewed report states the estimate.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas. The 25% figure is the weight loss that a systematic review reported by the American Society for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery found maintained for up to 10 years after surgery; population, duration and analysis follow SURMOUNT-1. No regulator or society sets a weight loss at which a medicine matches surgery.
completion.threshold_quote: Metabolic and bariatric surgery procedures gastric bypass and sleeve gastrectomy demonstrated total weight loss of 31.9% and 29.5% one year after surgery, respectively. Weight loss of approximately 25% was maintained for up to 10 years after surgery.
completion.basis: The Atlas uses the approximate 25% loss reported up to 10 years after gastric bypass or sleeve gastrectomy as a benchmark for magnitude. EMA’s current guideline recognizes a statistically significant placebo-corrected loss of at least 5% after 12 months. SURMOUNT-4’s 25.3% includes 36 weeks before randomization. TRIUMPH-1 reported 25.0% loss at 80 weeks for assignment to retatrutide 12 mg (95% CI, 24.0–26.0%), versus 3.9% with placebo. That point estimate meets the trial milestone. Retatrutide remains investigational.

milestones.title: An incretin agonist reduces body weight in obese mice versus vehicle at P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: During chronic treatment of mice with diet-induced obesity, the incretin agonist reduces body weight relative to vehicle at P<0.05 in a repeated-measures analysis of variance.
milestones.set_by: Coskun et al., Eli Lilly and collaborators, published preclinical experiment, Figure 3; an experiment-specific test.
milestones.threshold_quote: P < 0.05 using one-way ANOVA repeated measures versus the vehicle

milestones.title: An incretin agonist reduces human body weight versus placebo by day 29 at P<0.05.
milestones.criterion: In a placebo-controlled phase 1b trial in adults with type 2 diabetes, the mean change in body weight from baseline to day 29 favors the incretin agonist at P<0.05 in a mixed model for repeated measures. Body weight is a secondary pharmacodynamic endpoint.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly's phase 1b proof-of-concept study, reported by Coskun et al., clinical outcomes and Figure 5; written for adults with type 2 diabetes.
milestones.threshold_quote: Statistically significant at 5% significance level compared to placebo

milestones.title: People receiving an incretin agonist reach ≥10% weight loss at 26 weeks in a phase 2 trial.
milestones.criterion: A randomized phase 2 dose-ranging trial in adults with type 2 diabetes reports the proportion in each dose group who lose at least 10% of baseline body weight by week 26. The prespecified secondary endpoint uses on-treatment data from the modified intention-to-treat population. The protocol specifies the loss required of an individual responder and gives no minimum proportion of responders.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly, NCT03131687, secondary endpoint reported by Frías et al.; written for adults with type 2 diabetes.
milestones.threshold_quote: proportion of patients with at least 5% and 10% bodyweight loss from baseline to 26 weeks.

milestones.title: A phase 3 incretin trial beats placebo for ≥20% weight-loss responses at 72 weeks.
milestones.criterion: In a randomized phase 3 trial in adults without diabetes who have obesity or overweight with a weight-related complication, a greater proportion assigned to the incretin agonist than to placebo loses at least 20% of baseline body weight by week 72. The prespecified superiority comparison controls for multiple testing, as in the SURMOUNT-1 comparisons of tirzepatide 10 mg and 15 mg with placebo.
milestones.set_by: Eli Lilly, SURMOUNT-1 protocol NCT04184622, described in the SURMOUNT programme design paper; written for adults without diabetes.
milestones.threshold_quote: Key secondary end points include the proportion of participants achieving a body weight reduction ≥10%, ≥15%, or ≥20%

milestones.title: An FDA-approved obesity medicine produces at least 20% mean weight loss at 72 weeks in phase 3.
milestones.criterion: At a dose approved by the FDA for chronic weight management, a medicine produces mean loss of at least 20% of baseline body weight at week 72 in a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial. Participants are adults without type 2 diabetes who have obesity or overweight with a weight-related complication. The mean is estimated for all participants randomized to that dose, regardless of treatment discontinuation.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas; the former completion test. The 20% figure equals the goal the European Association for the Study of Obesity set in 2015 for individual patients with BMI of 35 kg/m² or more; no body sets it for a trial mean.
milestones.threshold_quote: A greater (20% or more) weight loss may be considered for those with greater degrees of obesity

milestones.title: A phase 3 trial shows at least 25% mean weight loss, counting participants who stopped treatment.
milestones.criterion: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial, adults without type 2 diabetes have obesity or overweight with a weight-related complication. At least 72 weeks after randomization, the estimated mean loss from randomization is at least 25% of baseline body weight in one assigned dose group, regardless of treatment discontinuation. Approval is not required. A sponsor announcement provides a claimed result pending peer-reviewed publication. An estimate reaching 25% only under the assumption of continued treatment provides partial evidence.
milestones.set_by: Technology Atlas; the completion figure without the approval. The 25% figure is from the systematic review reported by the American Society for Metabolic and Bariatric Surgery.
milestones.threshold_quote: Weight loss of approximately 25% was maintained for up to 10 years after surgery.

milestones.title: A pivotal trial shows at least 5% placebo-corrected weight loss after 12 months.
milestones.criterion: After 12 months of treatment, mean loss as a percentage of weight at randomization is at least 5 percentage points greater with the medicine than with placebo, and the between-group difference is statistically significant.
milestones.set_by: European Medicines Agency, Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use, Guideline on clinical evaluation of medicinal products used in weight management, section 4.1.
milestones.threshold_quote: statistically significant, placebo-corrected weight loss of at least 5% of baseline weight after 12 months of treatment

not_found: Coskun et al.'s supplementary DOCX could not be read, leaving the preclinical mouse group sizes unverified.
No regulator or professional society statement was found disputing the value or feasibility of developing an obesity medicine that reaches the surgical weight-loss benchmark.
